title: A graphic frame with a linked image
concept: How a Rectangle becomes a graphic frame by nesting an <Image> that references an external file via <Link LinkResourceURI>, plus the image's own ItemTransform.

annotations.note: The host is an ordinary Rectangle — the same element a colour swatch uses. What turns it into a graphic frame is the <Image> child below, not any attribute on the rectangle itself.

The nested <Image> carries its own ItemTransform (a b c d tx ty), here a half-scale. It maps the image's natural pixel space into the frame's inner coordinate space; the frame's own ItemTransform then carries that onto the page.

<Link LinkResourceURI> names the external file. The parser captures the URI string and defers the actual lookup to an AssetResolver at render time. A linked Link and an embedded <Contents> payload reach the parser the same way.
